state.context: Classify adversarial audit findings on a Kogen Intent package (a macOS Seatbelt write boundary for Build roles) before the Build. blocking = the Build would likely fail, or a wrong implementation would pass the proofs, or the package contradicts the Shaper's requirement; advisory = worth noting, no Build or acceptance impact.

findings.f1: Outcome 13 grants writes to the harness home, temp dir, raw-log dir, Keychain file, Claude refresh lock and most of the Codex scope, while the Shaper's rule says roles cannot write outside their Build's worktree.
findings.f2: The raw-log grant (KOGEN_RAW_LOG_DIR) is checked only for containing control, so it may sit inside control or another Candidate, and live fixtures default it inside the installing checkout.
findings.f3: inherited mode lets a nested Build launched from a role shell run with the outer Build's grants while claiming its own boundary, based on a role-controlled marker.
findings.f4: The live-reviewer-rework paid proof checks verdicts and a self-reported applied record but no attempted outside write from the real Codex process tree, so an implementation wrapping only fake Codex could pass.
findings.f5: Wrapping every fake role needs an inventory of existing fake roles' and hooks' write destinations; only two are named, while the earlier attempt failed 47 tests, and probe 9 was not a passing gate.
findings.a1: The no-escape claim is broader than the tested routes (other IPC/services, pre-existing hardlinks).
findings.a2: live-reviewer-rework is justified under D8 but its assertion is too weak.
findings.a3: Codex scope and Keychain grants are security exceptions and should be described as such.
findings.a4: No missing guarded paths or unexplained selectors.
findings.a5: D9 controller constraints are correctly identified and remain a build gate.
